findings.who: A partner whose only partnership loss is reported in Box 10 (net section 1231 loss) or Box 11 (other loss), with no negative amount in Boxes 1, 2, 3, 8, 9a, or 14A.
findings.why_no: The gate lists only Boxes 1, 2, 3, 8, 9a and 14A, so the tool computes no loss and never asks the gated questions.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 8: These losses and deductions include a loss on the disposition of assets and the section 179 expense deduction.
findings.fix: Broaden the gate to any partnership loss or deduction, including Box 10 and Box 11, not just the enumerated loss boxes.

findings.who: A partner whose only relevant K-1 item is a section 179 expense deduction in Box 12 and who has amounts in the activity for which they are not at risk.
findings.why_no: Box 12 is not one of the gate's listed boxes, so a section 179 deduction alone never opens the at-risk question.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 8: These losses and deductions include a loss on the disposition of assets and the section 179 expense deduction.
findings.fix: Broaden the gate to any loss or other deduction, including Box 12 section 179, and ask the at-risk question whenever such a deduction is present.

findings.who: A partner with only a charitable contribution in Box 13 or foreign taxes in Box 16 and insufficient adjusted basis to cover the contribution or tax.
findings.why_no: No listed loss box is negative, so the gate never asks about basis; even if asked, the question says losses, not deductions, so the filer would answer no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 3: a partner’s share of the adjusted basis in partnership charitable contributions ... and taxes ... is subject to this basis limitation.
findings.fix: Broaden the gate to deductions subject to basis limitation and ask whether losses or deductions exceed basis.

findings.who: A partner with a prior-year suspended partnership loss carried into 2025 and no current-year K-1 loss in any listed box.
findings.why_no: The gate looks only at current 2025 K-1 boxes; the prior-year disallowed loss is deducted in 2025 but is invisible to the gate.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 3: Any losses and deductions not allowed can be carried forward.
findings.fix: Ask whether any partnership loss carryforward is being claimed and broaden the gate to prior-year suspended losses.

findings.who: A joint filer whose spouse, not the filer, is the partner with the K-1 loss and insufficient basis or at-risk amount.
findings.why_no: The gated questions say your 2025 losses and what you put in, so the filer may answer no because the investment belongs to the spouse.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 3: a partner may only claim their share of a partnership loss ... to the extent it doesn’t exceed their adjusted basis.
findings.fix: Use you or your spouse in both gated questions and in any related gate wording.

findings.who: A partner whose basis is reduced by nondeductible expenses, depletion, or other decreases omitted from the help's parenthetical formula.
findings.why_no: The help says basis is what you put in, plus your share of its income and debts, less losses and money taken out, so the filer computes a higher basis and answers no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 3: Use the Worksheet for Adjusting the Basis of a Partner’s Interest in the Partnership to figure the basis of your interest.
findings.fix: Replace the incomplete formula with a instruction to use the Schedule K-1 basis worksheet and note that nondeductible expenses and other items reduce basis.

findings.who: A partner with a K-1 loss in a listed box whose activity was financed by partnership nonrecourse debt allocated to them, but who did not personally contribute borrowed money.
findings.why_no: The question asks whether what you put in was borrowed without personal liability; the partner truthfully reads no because the borrowing was by the partnership, not a contribution by them.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 8: Nonrecourse loans used to finance the activity, to acquire property used in the activity, or to acquire your interest in the activity that aren’t secured by your own property.
findings.fix: Ask about any nonrecourse partnership debt allocated to the partner or any amount in the activity not at risk, not only amounts the partner put in.

findings.who: A partner whose amount is protected by an indemnity, put, or other similar loss-protection arrangement that is not literally a guarantee or stop-loss agreement.
findings.why_no: The question lists only a guarantee or stop-loss agreement, so the filer reads the list as complete and answers no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 8: protected against loss by a guarantee, a stop-loss agreement, or other similar arrangement.
findings.fix: Add or other similar arrangement to the question.

findings.who: A partner with a nonrecourse real-estate loan that is not qualified nonrecourse financing, for example a loan from a related party, but who sees it as a real-estate loan.
findings.why_no: The parenthetical other than qualified real estate loans invites the filer to treat any real-estate loan as excepted, though only qualified nonrecourse financing secured by real property is excepted.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 8: See the instructions for item K1, later, for the exception for qualified nonrecourse financing secured by real property.
findings.fix: Ask whether the loan is qualified nonrecourse financing secured by real property, or ask a broad yes and classify later from the instructions.

locators: p. 3, Basis Limitations, "a partner may only claim their share of a partnership loss (including a capital loss) to the extent it doesn’t exceed their adjusted basis in the partnership"
p. 3, Limitations on Losses, Deductions, and Credits, "the basis limitations, the at-risk limitations, the passive activity limitations, and the excess business loss limitations"
p. 8, At-Risk Limitations, "you’ll have to complete Form 6198, At-Risk Limitations, to figure your allowable loss for the activity"

findings.who: A general partner with a box 2 rental real estate loss who actively participated only by arranging for others to provide services, such as hiring or coordinating a plumber or repair contractor, in a significant and bona fide sense, but who did not approve tenants, rents, or repairs.
findings.why_no: The question asks whether they 'help make decisions' and gives examples of approving tenants, rents, or repairs; arranging services is not described as a decision, so they truthfully answer no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 11: 'You may be treated as actively participating if you participated, for example, in making management decisions or arranging for others to provide services (such as repairs) in a significant and bona fide sense.'
findings.fix: Ask whether the filer participated in making management decisions or arranging for others to provide services in a significant and bona fide sense, not only whether they helped make decisions.

findings.who: A general partner with a box 2 rental real estate loss who approved a capital expenditure (for example, a new roof or HVAC system), decided lease terms other than the rent amount, or made another similar management decision, but did not do one of the examples in the question.
findings.why_no: The question lists 'approving tenants, rents or repairs' and omits capital expenditures, rental terms generally, and 'other similar decisions'; the filer reads the list as complete and answers no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 11: 'Management decisions that can count as active participation include approving new tenants, deciding rental terms, approving capital or repair expenditures, and other similar decisions.'
findings.fix: Use the full statutory examples and add 'or other similar management decisions, including approving capital expenditures or deciding rental terms,' or ask broadly about any management decision.

findings.who: A general partner whose box 2 covers more than one rental real estate activity and who helped make decisions for one activity but not another.
findings.why_no: The question asks about 'its rental real estate' in the singular without saying 'any activity'; the filer reads it as asking whether they helped with all of the partnership's rental real estate and answers no because they did not help with every activity.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 11: 'Special allowance for a rental real estate activity' and 'If you have net income (loss), deductions, or credits from any activity to which special rules apply, the partnership will identify the activity and all amounts relating to it on Schedule K-1 or on an attached statement.'
findings.fix: Ask per rental real estate activity, or clarify 'any of its rental real estate activities' and capture which activity the filer participated in.

findings.who: A sole general partner who personally made all management decisions for the rental real estate without assistance from anyone else.
findings.why_no: The word 'help' can be read as assisting someone else; a sole decision-maker may say they did not 'help' make decisions, they made them alone, and answer no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 11: 'You may be treated as actively participating if you participated, for example, in making management decisions...'
findings.fix: Ask 'Did you participate in making management decisions...' rather than 'Did you help make decisions...'

locators: p. 11, Special allowance for a rental real estate activity, "Limited partners can’t actively participate unless future regulations provide an exception"

p. 11, Special allowance for a rental real estate activity, "Management decisions that can count as active participation include approving new tenants, deciding rental terms, approving capital or repair expenditures"

findings.who: A partner receives a K-1 for a rental activity subject to the special dwelling-use rule, but boxes 2 and 3 are blank or zero because the K-1 reports only separately stated deductions or credits from that activity.
findings.why_no: The computed gate looks only for an amount in box 2 or box 3, so it is false and the tool never asks the personal-use question.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 11: 'If you have net income (loss), deductions, or credits from any of the following activities, treat such amounts as nonpassive' and item 2 covers 'The rental of a dwelling unit any partner used for personal purposes during the year for more than the greater of 14 days or 10%...'
findings.fix: Broaden the gate to any K-1 or attached statement identifying a rental dwelling special activity, including deductions and credits, not only nonzero boxes 2 or 3.

findings.who: A partner in a partnership with multiple rental activities gets a K-1 whose box 2/3 net total is blank or zero, while an attached statement identifies one personally used dwelling activity with income subject to recharacterization.
findings.why_no: The gate tests only the face of boxes 2 and 3; if the special activity is reported on an attached statement or netted to zero with another activity, the tool computes false and suppresses the question.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 11: 'The partnership will identify the activity and all amounts relating to it on Schedule K-1 or on an attached statement.'
findings.fix: Check attached statements and activity-level amounts, not merely the net amount printed in boxes 2 and 3.

findings.who: A partner personally used a partnership dwelling unit that is not naturally called a 'rental home'—for example, an apartment, mobile home, or boat—for more than the statutory threshold, and the K-1 has a box 2 or 3 amount.
findings.why_no: The question and help say 'rental homes'; the filer reads that as excluding their dwelling unit and answers no, although the IRS text uses the broader term 'dwelling unit'.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 11: 'The rental of a dwelling unit any partner used for personal purposes...'
findings.fix: Use 'dwelling unit' and list examples (house, apartment, condominium, mobile home, boat, or similar property) instead of 'rental home'.

findings.who: A partner in a fiscal-year partnership whose 2025 K-1 covers a tax year beginning in 2024; the partner used the dwelling personally in late 2024 during that partnership tax year.
findings.why_no: The question says 'In 2025'; the filer answers no because the personal use occurred in 2024, even though it was during the partnership's tax year covered by the K-1.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 11: 'The rental of a dwelling unit any partner used for personal purposes during the year...'
findings.fix: Ask about 'during the partnership's tax year shown on this K-1,' not calendar year 2025.

findings.who: A partner used a dwelling personally more than 14 days, but the dwelling had zero fair-rental days (for example, all rental days were below fair rent or it was not rented at fair rental value).
findings.why_no: The filer reads 'over a tenth of the days it was rented at a fair price' as requiring some fair-price rental days and answers no when there are none, though the statutory threshold is the greater of 14 days or 10% of fair-rental days, so 14 days controls.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 11: 'more than the greater of 14 days or 10% of the number of days that the residence was rented at fair rental value.'
findings.fix: State the statutory formula directly and clarify that if there are no fair-rental days, the 14-day threshold applies alone.

locators: p. 11, Special rules for certain other activities, "The rental of a dwelling unit any partner used for personal purposes during the year for more than the greater of 14 days or 10% of the number of days that the residence was rented at fair rental value"

findings.who: A partner in a partnership with more than one activity (the K-1 has the required activity statement) who materially participated for 5 of 2015-2024 in the trade or business activity that produced the Box 1 ordinary business income, but not in the partnership's other activity.
findings.why_no: The question asks about 'this business' in the singular and the help refers to 'the business's income or loss'; the filer reads it as requiring material participation in the partnership as a whole, so answers no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'If the partnership had more than one activity, it’ll attach a statement ... identifies each activity ... Material participation. You must determine if you materially participated ... in each trade or business activity held through the partnership'
findings.fix: Ask the test-5 question separately for each activity identified on the K-1 statement, or word it as the activity that produced the Box 1 amount.

findings.who: A limited partner who did not work in 2025 but materially participated in the partnership activity for 5 of 2015-2024.
findings.why_no: The citation and heading given with the question say 'Individuals (other than limited partners),' so the filer reads the question as not applying to limited partners and answers no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'Limited partners. If you’re a limited partner, you must meet item 1, 5, or 6 above to qualify as having materially participated.'
findings.fix: Cite or state the limited-partner rule and tell limited partners they can meet test 5.

findings.who: A partner who materially participated in the business for 5 of 2015-2024, but whose earlier returns do not show an income or loss entry in Schedule E columns (i) or (k) because the activity had no income/loss or the losses were suspended.
findings.why_no: The help says 'Your earlier returns show it: the business's income or loss was in column (i) or (k) of Schedule E, not (g) or (h)'; seeing no such entry, the filer answers no even though test 5 depends on participation, not on an entry.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'You materially participated in the activity for any 5 tax years (whether or not consecutive) during the 10 tax years that immediately precede the tax year.'
findings.fix: Say the earlier returns may show it but are not required; ask about participation or nonpassive treatment rather than only column entries.

findings.who: A filer whose spouse materially participated in the partnership activity for 5 of 2015-2024, but the spouse filed separate returns in those years, so the filer's own earlier returns do not show the business in Schedule E columns (i) or (k).
findings.why_no: The question includes 'or your spouse,' but the help says 'Your earlier returns show it'; the filer checks only their own returns, sees no entry, and answers no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'Generally, any work that you or your spouse does in connection with an activity held through a partnership ... is counted toward material participation.' and test 5's 5-of-10 rule.
findings.fix: Make the help refer to the spouse's returns too and to the spouse's work, not only the filer's Schedule E columns.

findings.who: A real estate professional who materially participated for 5 of 2015-2024 in a partnership's rental real estate activity, and whose K-1 shows Box 2 rental income but no Box 1 ordinary business income.
findings.why_no: The gate requires Box 1 ordinary business income; with Box 1 blank, the tool never asks the test-5 question and treats the line as false.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'You must determine if you materially participated (a) in each trade or business activity held through the partnership, and (b) if you were a real estate professional (defined earlier) in each rental real estate activity held through the partnership.'
findings.fix: Broaden the gate to any activity amount (Box 1, Box 2, etc.) or ask the test-5 question per activity, including rental real estate for a real estate professional.

findings.who: A partner who materially participated in 2015, 2017, 2018, 2020, and 2022, but not in five consecutive years.
findings.why_no: The question says 'In at least 5 of the years 2015 to 2024' and omits the instructions' 'whether or not consecutive'; the filer reads it as requiring five consecutive years and answers no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'You materially participated in the activity for any 5 tax years (whether or not consecutive) during the 10 tax years that immediately precede the tax year.'
findings.fix: Add 'whether or not consecutive' to the question.

locators: p. 9, Individuals (other than limited partners), "You materially participated in the activity for any 5 tax years (whether or not consecutive) during the 10 tax years that immediately precede the tax year"

findings.who: A sole general partner who worked 90 hours while an employee worked 10 hours; no other individual participated, so the filer did substantially all the work but was not less than someone else.
findings.why_no: The gate requires that the general partner worked 'less than someone else.' Because the filer worked more than the employee and no one else worked more, that is false, so the tool never asks the nearly-all question.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'Your participation in the activity for the tax year constituted substantially all the participation in the activity of all individuals (including individuals who aren’t owners of interests in the activity).'
findings.fix: Do not require 'less than someone else'; ask the nearly-all test whenever test 3 is not met, including when participation is 100 hours or less and the filer did substantially all the work.

findings.who: A limited partner who owned a general partnership interest at all times during 2025 and did substantially all the work with 100 hours or less, such as 90 hours with one employee at 10.
findings.why_no: The gate says 'A general partner'; this filer is a limited partner, so they truthfully answer no even though the IRS treats a limited partner who owned a general partnership interest at all times under the same material-participation tests, including test 2.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'Individuals (other than limited partners). If you’re an individual (either a general partner or a limited partner who owned a general partnership interest at all times during the tax year), you materially participated ...' and test 2: 'constituted substantially all the participation in the activity of all individuals.'
findings.fix: Broaden the gate from 'general partner' to any individual other than a limited partner, expressly including a limited partner who owned a general partnership interest at all times.

findings.who: A joint filer whose spouse is the general partner and whose combined work is 100 hours or less and substantially all the activity's participation, such as spouse 90 hours and filer 10 hours.
findings.why_no: The gate asks about 'A general partner who worked' and checks the filer’s own status and hours; the filer is not the general partner, and the general-partner spouse is not 'less than someone else' because the filer worked less. The tool skips the question, though the gated question asks about 'you (and your spouse)' and the IRS counts spousal work.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'Generally, any work that you or your spouse does in connection with an activity held through a partnership ... is counted toward material participation.'
findings.fix: Apply the gate to 'you or your spouse' and use combined spousal status and hours, matching the gated question and the IRS spouse rule.

locators: p. 9, Individuals (other than limited partners), "constituted substantially all the participation in the activity of all individuals"

findings.who: A partner in an unlisted personal-service trade or business where capital is not a material income-producing factor, such as an advertising agency, public-relations firm, insurance agency, or similar service business outside the parenthetical fields.
findings.why_no: The question lists only health, law, engineering, architecture, accounting, actuarial science, performing arts, and consulting; the filer reads that list as the whole definition and says no because their business is not one of those named fields.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'A personal service activity involves the performance of personal services in the field of health, law, engineering, architecture, accounting, actuarial science, performing arts, or consulting, or any other trade or business in which capital isn’t a material income-producing factor.'
findings.fix: Add the catch-all 'or any other trade or business in which capital isn’t a material income-producing factor' to the question, or ask whether the activity is a personal service activity and show the full definition.

findings.who: A filer with a single Schedule K-1 that reports more than one activity, only one of which is a personal service activity in which they materially participated for any 3 earlier years.
findings.why_no: The question says 'On this Schedule K-1 — Is it a service business' at the form level, so the filer answers no because the K-1 as a whole includes a non-service activity, even though the IRS requires the determination activity by activity.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'If the partnership had more than one activity, it’ll attach a statement to your Schedule K-1 that identifies each activity' and 'You must determine if you materially participated (a) in each trade or business activity held through the partnership'.
findings.fix: Ask the question per activity, using the attached statement, and word it 'For this activity' rather than 'On this Schedule K-1'.

findings.who: A filer whose Schedule K-1 has no Box 1 amount but has a deduction or credit, such as Box 13 credits, from a personal service activity in which they materially participated for any 3 earlier years.
findings.why_no: The gate itself requires 'Box 1 shows an amount'; with Box 1 zero, the computed condition is false, so the tool never asks the test-6 question and treats the gated line as no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'Income (loss), deductions, and credits from an activity are nonpassive if you determine that: • You materially participated in a trade or business activity of the partnership'.
findings.fix: Broaden the gate to ask whenever the K-1 reports any income, loss, deduction, or credit affected by material participation, not only when Box 1 has an amount.

locators: p. 9, Individuals (other than limited partners), "The activity was a personal service activity and you materially participated in the activity for any 3 tax years"
p. 9, Material participation, "You must determine if you materially participated (a) in each trade or business activity held through the partnership"

findings.who: A joint filer who is a general partner but did not personally work in the partnership in 2025; the filer's spouse did the work, or the spouse is the general partner whose K-1 is on the joint return.
findings.why_no: The gate says 'A general partner who worked' and uses 'you' without 'or your spouse', so the filer truthfully says no; the gated questions expressly count the spouse's work.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'Generally, any work that you or your spouse does in connection with an activity held through a partnership ... is counted toward material participation.'
findings.fix: Gate on 'you or your spouse is a general partner and you or your spouse worked during the partnership's tax year', not on the filer's own work alone.

findings.who: A limited partner who owned a general partnership interest at all times during the partnership tax year and worked enough to meet test 4 or test 7; the K-1 item G is 'Limited partner or other LLC member' rather than general partner/LLC member-manager.
findings.why_no: They read 'general partner' and item G 'Limited partner' as excluding them, so they answer no, although the IRS puts a limited partner who owned a GP interest at all times under the individuals-other-than-limited-partners standards.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'If you’re an individual (either a general partner or a limited partner who owned a general partnership interest at all times during the tax year), you materially participated ... only if one or more of the following apply.'
findings.fix: Broaden item G/gate to include a limited partner who owned a general partnership interest at all times; ask that fact rather than relying only on item G.

findings.who: A general partner with no Box 1 amount (zero, blank, or net zero with activity amounts on the attached statement) but with passive deductions or credits in other K-1 boxes, such as Box 2, 13, or 23, who met test 4 or test 7.
findings.why_no: The gate is computed as 'Box 1 shows an amount' and is false, so the tool never asks t4/t7 and treats them as no; the filer's material participation still matters to the other activity amounts.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'If you determine that you didn’t materially participate ... the amounts from that activity are passive. Report passive income (losses), deductions, and credits ...'
findings.fix: Do not require a Box 1 amount; ask material-participation questions whenever the K-1 has any activity income, loss, deduction, or credit whose passive/nonpassive character depends on material participation, or ask per activity.

findings.who: A general partner whose partnership has a fiscal tax year and who worked more than 500 hours (or regular, continuous, and substantial) during that partnership tax year but not in calendar 2025, e.g. work from July-December 2024 for a July 2024-June 2025 tax year.
findings.why_no: They read 'worked in the business in 2025' as calendar 2025 and answer no; the IRS measures participation by the partnership's tax year, not calendar 2025.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'All determinations of material participation are based on your participation during the partnership’s tax year.'
findings.fix: Use 'during the partnership's tax year shown on this K-1' instead of 'in 2025' in the gate.

findings.who: A general partner with one K-1 covering more than one activity, who met test 1 (or another of tests 1, 2, 3, 5) in one activity but met none of those tests and met test 4 or test 7 in another activity.
findings.why_no: The gate asks 'met none of tests 1, 2, 3 and 5' at the K-1 level; because they met test 1 in one activity, they truthfully answer no for the K-1, so t4/t7 are never asked for the other activity.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'If the partnership had more than one activity, it’ll attach a statement ... Material participation. You must determine if you materially participated ... in each trade or business activity held through the partnership.'
findings.fix: Ask the gate and the material-participation questions separately for each activity identified on the attached statement, not once for the whole K-1.

findings.who: A general partner in a rental real estate activity who is a real estate professional and met test 4 or test 7 through work in that rental activity.
findings.why_no: The gate says 'worked in the business'; the filer reads rental real estate as not a 'business' and answers no, although a real estate professional must test material participation in each rental real estate activity and can use tests 4 and 7.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'You must determine if you materially participated (a) in each trade or business activity held through the partnership, and (b) if you were a real estate professional ... in each rental real estate activity held through the partnership.'
findings.fix: Say 'trade or business activity, or rental real estate activity if you were a real estate professional' rather than only 'the business'.

locators: p. 9, Individuals (other than limited partners), "Based on all the facts and circumstances, you participated in the activity on a regular, continuous, and substantial basis during the tax year"
p. 9, Individuals (other than limited partners), "The activity was a significant participation activity for the tax year"
p. 9, Limited partners, "If you’re a limited partner, you must meet item 1, 5, or 6 above to qualify as having materially participated"

findings.who: A filer whose held-back rental loss built up over several years, for example from 2019 through 2024. They actively participated only from 2022 on. Before that they held the interest passively or were not involved in decisions.
findings.why_no: "The held-back rental real estate loss" reads as last year's single carryover. Form 8582 Part VII column (c) pools all prior years into one figure, so the filer checks only 2024, when they did participate, and answers no without looking at the older years inside the amount.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part IV: "Don't enter a prior-year unallowed loss in column (c) of Part IV unless you actively participated in the activity in both the year the loss arose and the current tax year."
findings.fix: Ask: "The held-back loss may include losses from several earlier years. For any of those years, did you not help make decisions for this rental, or own less than a tenth of it at any time that year?" Help: "Check every year whose loss is still carried forward, not only last year."

findings.who: A married filer who filed separately in the year the loss arose and lived with their spouse at some point that year. They made the management decisions and owned well over 10%.
findings.why_no: The question asks only about decisions and ownership. Both were true for this filer, so they answer no. Married filing separately while living with a spouse also disqualifies that year from the active participation rule, and the question never mentions it.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part IV Caution: "Married individuals who file separate returns and lived with their spouses at any time during the tax year don't qualify under the active participation rule and must use Part V instead of Part IV."
findings.fix: Add a separate question: "In any year the held-back loss arose, did you file married filing separately and live with your spouse at any time that year?" Treat a yes the same as a yes to the participation question.

findings.who: A filer who in a loss year owned 10% or more for most of the year but fell below a tenth for part of it. Another example is a filer who held the interest as a limited partner that year and still weighed in on decisions informally.
findings.why_no: "Owned less than a tenth of it" without "at any time" reads as the year-end or typical share. "Help make decisions" invites a limited partner who gave informal input to answer no.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part IV: "unless you actively participated in the activity in both the year the loss arose and the current tax year. If you didn't actively participate in both years, enter the prior-year unallowed loss in column (c) of Part V."
findings.fix: Ask: "…or owned less than a tenth of it (counting your spouse's share) at any time that year, or held it only as a limited partner?"

findings.who: Any filer who is unsure how to answer.
findings.why_no: The help says "A Yes ends the interview here." That pushes an uncertain filer toward no to keep going, and a no silently places the prior-year loss in Part IV.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part IV: "If you didn't actively participate in both years, enter the prior-year unallowed loss in column (c) of Part V."
findings.fix: Replace the help with what the answer decides: "If yes, part of this loss belongs in Part V and can't use the special allowance. This tool can't split it, so a yes stops here."

findings.who: A joint filer whose spouse made the rental decisions, or held the larger share, in the loss year. The filer personally did neither.
findings.why_no: The singular "you" leads this filer to answer yes, the opposite error. The interview is wrongly refused even though their spouse's participation and share can count toward the requirement.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part IV: "unless you actively participated in the activity in both the year the loss arose and the current tax year"
findings.fix: Ask: "…a year when neither you nor your spouse helped make decisions for it, or the two of you together owned less than a tenth of it?"

locators: p. 10, Part IV, "Don’t enter a prior-year unallowed loss in column (c) of Part IV unless you actively participated in the activity in both the year the loss arose and the current tax year"

findings.who: A filer with a Box 2 amount who is a real estate professional and materially participated in the partnership rental real estate, and who also rents out a separate duplex or vacation home, or receives oil-and-gas or other royalties.
findings.why_no: They truthfully answer yes to the parent scope question 'did you rent out ... anything you own or lease, or receive royalties'; the computed gate requires no rental or royalty of their own, so the K-1 re_pro question is skipped and the gated line is silently set to No.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 14: 'the income (loss) in box 2 isn’t from a passive activity if you were a real estate professional ... and you materially participated in the activity'
findings.fix: Drop the 'no rental or royalty of your own' condition and ask the K-1 Box 2 real-estate-professional/material-participation question whenever Box 2 shows an amount.

findings.who: On a joint return, a filer with a Box 2 amount who is a real estate professional and materially participated in the partnership rental real estate, while the spouse separately rents out a property or receives royalties.
findings.why_no: The parent scope question includes the spouse, so the filer truthfully answers yes because of the spouse's rental or royalty; the computed gate becomes false and the filer's own K-1 re_pro line is set to No.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 14: 'the income (loss) in box 2 isn’t from a passive activity if you were a real estate professional ... and you materially participated in the activity'
findings.fix: Do not let a spouse's unrelated rental or royalty activity suppress the K-1 Box 2 real-estate-professional question; ask it based on the Box 2 activity and the filer's or spouse's real-estate-professional hours.

findings.who: A filer with a Box 2 amount who is a real estate professional and materially participated, but who does not personally own or lease rental real estate; they see the K-1's 'net rental real estate income' and believe they rented out a property.
findings.why_no: They answer yes to the scope helper because the K-1 reports rental real estate income, so the tool treats the gate as false and skips the K-1 re_pro question; the property is actually owned by the partnership, not the filer.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 14: 'the income (loss) in box 2 isn’t from a passive activity if you were a real estate professional ... and you materially participated in the activity'
findings.fix: Clarify that the scope helper asks only about rental or royalty activities owned or leased directly by the filer or spouse, not a partnership's rental real estate reported in Box 2; or remove the condition.

findings.who: A filer who materially participated in the partnership's Box 2 rental real estate but whose more-than-750 real-estate hours are in another real estate business, such as brokerage or construction, not in the K-1 partnership.
findings.why_no: They read 'On this Schedule K-1' as asking whether they worked more than 750 hours for this partnership and answer no, although the real estate professional test counts hours in any real property trade or business and the Box 2 activity only needs material participation.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 14: 'the income (loss) in box 2 isn’t from a passive activity if you were a real estate professional ... and you materially participated in the activity'
findings.fix: Ask the real-estate-professional hours question without limiting it to this K-1 activity, and ask material participation in the Box 2 activity separately.

findings.who: On a joint return, one spouse meets the real estate professional tests (for example, 800 real-estate hours and 100 other work hours), but the other spouse has 1,000 hours of non-real-estate work; the filer with the Box 2 amount materially participated.
findings.why_no: They read 'more than half of all your work time' as combined household work time, so 800/1,900 fails; the real estate professional test is applied spouse-by-spouse, and the qualifying spouse makes the answer yes.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 14: 'the income (loss) in box 2 isn’t from a passive activity if you were a real estate professional ... and you materially participated in the activity'
findings.fix: State that on a joint return either spouse may qualify separately; do not combine the spouses' work hours for the more-than-half test.

locators: p. 14, Box 2. Net Rental Real Estate Income (Loss), "the income (loss) in box 2 isn’t from a passive activity if you were a real estate professional (defined earlier) and you materially participated in the activity"

findings.who: A general partner with a box 2 rental real estate amount who did not personally make management decisions but arranged for others to provide services, such as repairs, in a significant and bona fide way.
findings.why_no: The gate asks only whether the filer 'Helped make management decisions'; arranging for repair or other services is not itself a management decision, so the filer answers no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 11: 'You may be treated as actively participating if you participated, for example, in making management decisions or arranging for others to provide services (such as repairs) in a significant and bona fide sense.'
findings.fix: Broaden the gate to ask whether the filer participated in management decisions or arranged for others to provide services in a significant and bona fide sense.

findings.who: A member of an LLC taxed as a partnership who actively manages the LLC’s rental real estate and owns at least 10% by value all year, but who is not formally a general partner because the LLC has members, not general partners.
findings.why_no: The gate is computed only when 'the partner is a general partner'; an LLC member is not a general partner, so the tool sets the gate false without asking about management or 10% ownership.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 11: 'Limited partners can’t actively participate unless future regulations provide an exception' and 'You may be treated as actively participating if you participated, for example, in making management decisions...'
findings.fix: Gate on whether the filer is a limited partner or on actual participation, not on the 'general partner' label; allow LLC members and other non-limited partners to answer.

findings.who: A general partner whose rental real estate income or loss is identified on an attached statement rather than entered in box 2 of the Schedule K-1.
findings.why_no: The gate requires 'Box 2 shows an amount'; when the amount is on the attached statement and box 2 is blank, the tool computes the gate false and never asks the 10% question.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 11: 'If you have net income (loss), deductions, or credits from any activity to which special rules apply, the partnership will identify the activity and all amounts relating to it on Schedule K-1 or on an attached statement.'
findings.fix: Gate on any rental real estate activity amount reported on the K-1 or an attached statement, not only an amount printed in box 2.

findings.who: A joint filer who is the general partner with a box 2 amount but personally did not help make management decisions; the filer’s spouse made the management decisions for the rental real estate.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether 'you' helped make management decisions and does not say 'you or your spouse,' so the filer answers no for themselves even though the spouse’s participation is on the joint return.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 11: 'your interest (including your spouse’s interest) in the activity' and 'You may be treated as actively participating if you participated...'
findings.fix: Ask 'Did you or your spouse help make management decisions...?' and apply the participation test to either spouse on a joint return.

findings.who: A joint filer whose own interest is 5% but whose spouse owns another 5% in the same rental real estate activity, so combined they meet the 10% test; the filer reads the help 'The partnership’s records or item J show your share' as looking only at their own share.
findings.why_no: The help says 'your share' and tells them to answer no if it was less than a tenth, omitting the spouse’s share even though the question includes the spouse.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 11: 'your interest (including your spouse’s interest) in the activity was less than 10% (by value) of all interests in the activity.'
findings.fix: Change the help to say to include the spouse’s interest and use the combined capital/value percentage, not just the filer’s own share.

findings.who: A general partner with a box 2 amount who did not negotiate leases or approve tenants, but did approve capital or repair expenditures for the rental real estate.
findings.why_no: The gate says 'Helped make management decisions'; the filer reads that as tenant or lease decisions and does not realize that approving repairs or capital expenditures counts, so answers no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 11: 'Management decisions that can count as active participation include approving new tenants, deciding rental terms, approving capital or repair expenditures, and other similar decisions.'
findings.fix: Show those examples in the gate help or ask directly whether the filer approved tenants, rental terms, capital or repair expenditures, or other similar decisions.

findings.who: A general partner with a box 2 amount who owns at least 10% by capital or value but whose item J profit-sharing percentage is less than 10%; the filer uses the profit percentage because the help says item J shows 'your share.'
findings.why_no: The help does not say to use the capital/value percentage; using the profit or loss percentage makes the filer answer no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 11: 'your interest (including your spouse’s interest) in the activity was less than 10% (by value) of all interests in the activity.'
findings.fix: Specify that the test is by value/capital interest and tell filers which item J percentage to use, rather than simply saying 'your share.'

findings.who: A general partner with a box 2 rental real estate amount who owns 10% or more of the partnership but does not directly own the real estate; the filer reads 'own at least a tenth of all the interests in that rental real estate' as requiring direct ownership of the property.
findings.why_no: The question and help refer to owning interests in 'that rental real estate'; a lay filer may answer no because the partnership, not the filer, owns the property.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 11: 'your interest ... in the activity was less than 10% (by value) of all interests in the activity.'
findings.fix: Ask whether the filer’s interest in the partnership/rental real estate activity was at least 10% by value, and clarify that indirect partnership ownership counts.

locators: p. 11, Special allowance for a rental real estate activity, "Management decisions that can count as active participation include approving new tenants, deciding rental terms, approving capital or repair expenditures"
p. 11, Special allowance for a rental real estate activity, "your interest (including your spouse’s interest) in the activity was less than 10% (by value) of all interests in the activity"

findings.who: A limited partner who owned a general partnership interest at all times during the partnership’s tax year and worked more than 100 hours in the activity, at least as many as any other individual; Schedule K-1 item G is not checked because the filer is a limited partner.
findings.why_no: The filer reads 'General partner or LLC member-manager (item G)' as asking only about a general partner and answers no because they are a limited partner, so the gate never asks the 100-hour test.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'Individuals (other than limited partners). If you’re an individual (either a general partner or a limited partner who owned a general partnership interest at all times during the tax year), you materially participated ... 3. You participated in the activity for more than 100 hours ... and your participation ... wasn’t less than the participation ... of any other individual...'
findings.fix: Gate on item G or on a limited partner who owned a general partnership interest at all times; ask the GP-interest fact separately instead of relying on 'general partner' alone.

findings.who: A general partner in a partnership with two activities on one K-1 who worked 600 hours total (200 in Activity A and 400 in Activity B) and no one worked more than 200 in Activity A; the filer answers the 500-hour-or-less helper no because the total is 600.
findings.why_no: The filer reads 'worked in the business, 500 hours or less' at the K-1 or total level; 600 is not 500 or less, so the gate is skipped even though Activity A is 500 or less.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'If the partnership had more than one activity ... You must determine if you materially participated ... in each trade or business activity ... 3. You participated in the activity for more than 100 hours ... and your participation ... wasn’t less than the participation ... of any other individual...'
findings.fix: Ask the 500-hour and 100-hour tests per activity identified on the attached statement, not once for the K-1 total.

findings.who: A general partner in a partnership with two activities on one K-1 who worked 200 hours in Activity A (no one more in A) and 300 hours in Activity B (another individual worked 400 in B); total is 500 or less.
findings.why_no: The filer reads 'On this Schedule K-1 ... work in it ... at least as many as anyone else' as one K-1-wide question and answers no because in Activity B another individual worked more, though Activity A qualifies under test 3.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'If the partnership had more than one activity ... You must determine if you materially participated ... in each trade or business activity ... 3. You participated in the activity for more than 100 hours ... and your participation ... wasn’t less than the participation ... of any other individual...'
findings.fix: Ask per activity or add 'in any one activity' and identify the activity on the attached statement.

findings.who: A general partner in a partnership with a fiscal tax year, such as July 2024 through June 2025, who worked 200 hours in 2024 during the partnership year and none in calendar 2025, with no one working more.
findings.why_no: The gated question asks 'in 2025'; the filer answers no for calendar 2025, though the IRS test uses the partnership’s tax year.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'All determinations of material participation are based on your participation during the partnership’s tax year.'
findings.fix: Ask about participation during the partnership’s tax year and capture the partnership year begin and end dates instead of hard-coding 2025.

findings.who: A married general partner whose spouse worked 300 hours while the filer worked 0, or each spouse worked 200 while an employee worked 300; no one else exceeded the combined spousal hours.
findings.why_no: The gate helper asks whether the filer worked 500 hours or less, and the gated question asks whether 'you (or your spouse)' worked more than 100 and at least as many as anyone else; the filer answers no because they personally did not work or because neither individual was the maximum, though the IRS counts the spouse’s work with theirs.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'Generally, any work that you or your spouse does in connection with an activity held through a partnership ... is counted toward material participation.'
findings.fix: Ask for the combined filer-and-spouse hours and compare that combined total to any other individual; do not require one individual to be the maximum.

findings.who: A real estate professional general partner in a partnership rental real estate activity who worked 200 hours in the activity and no one worked more; the filer reads 'worked in the business' as excluding rental real estate.
findings.why_no: The filer answers no to the helper 'worked in the business, 500 hours or less' because the activity is rental real estate, so the gate never asks the 100-hour test.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'if you were a real estate professional (defined earlier) in each rental real estate activity held through the partnership' and test 3 applies to individuals other than limited partners.
findings.fix: Say 'activity, including rental real estate activity' and ask about participation, not only work in a business.

locators: p. 9, Individuals (other than limited partners), "You participated in the activity for more than 100 hours during the tax year, and your participation in the activity for the tax year wasn’t less than the participation in the activity of any other individual"
p. 9, Limited partners, "If you’re a limited partner, you must meet item 1, 5, or 6 above to qualify as having materially participated"

findings.who: A partner with a loss suspended on a 2024 Form 8582 whose 2025 K-1 shows nothing in boxes 1, 2 or 3. For example, the partnership broke even, or its only 2025 items are in other boxes (box 10 section 1231 gain or loss, box 11 other income, box 12 section 179, box 13 deductions).
findings.why_no: The tool computes the gate from current-year boxes 1-3 only. With all three blank or zero the gate is false, and the prior-year question is never asked.
findings.irs_text: "Column (c). Enter the prior-year unallowed losses for each activity. You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582." (i8582 2025 p. 10, Parts IV and V). The column takes the carryover with no condition on current-year income or loss.
findings.fix: Drop the box 1-3 gate. Ask k1p.prior_any for every Schedule K-1 (Form 1065), or gate it on 'any amount on this K-1 or any loss from this partnership on a 2024 Form 8582, Part VII'. The cited text does not support the gate condition.

findings.who: A partner who sold or otherwise fully disposed of the whole partnership interest in 2025, or whose partnership ended. The final K-1 shows zero in boxes 1-3, and the sale is reported elsewhere (Form 4797 or Form 8949).
findings.why_no: No box 1-3 amount on the final K-1 makes the computed gate false, so the suspended passive loss for the activity is set to zero. This is the year that loss matters most.
findings.irs_text: "Enter the prior-year unallowed losses for each activity." (i8582 2025 p. 10, Part V column (c)). Prior-year unallowed losses stay attached to the activity whatever its current-year boxes show.
findings.fix: Ask about prior-year unallowed losses whether or not any K-1 box has an amount, and ask separately whether the interest was disposed of in 2025.

findings.who: A partner whose box 1, 2 or 3 shows 'STMT', '*' or 'See attached' with no figure. The amounts are on a statement because the partnership has several activities.
findings.why_no: The helper asks whether 'Box 1 ... shows an amount'. The box itself shows no number, so the filer answers no for each box and the gate is false.
findings.irs_text: "Column (c). Enter the prior-year unallowed losses for each activity." (i8582 2025 p. 10)
findings.fix: Word each helper as 'Box N, or a statement attached for box N, shows an amount (other than zero)'. Better, remove the gate as in the first finding.

findings.who: Joint filers where the K-1 belongs to the spouse, and the spouse's loss was suspended on the spouse's own 2024 return (filed single or married filing separately before the joint return).
findings.why_no: The question says 'held back ... on your 2024 return'. The filer answering looks at the joint return or their own 2024 return, finds no such loss, and answers no.
findings.irs_text: "You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582." (i8582 2025 p. 10)
findings.fix: Ask: 'Was a loss from this partnership held back (not deducted) on your or your spouse's 2024 return or an earlier one, including a separate return, because of the passive activity rules?'

findings.who: A partner whose 2024 return had no Form 8582 attached (prepared elsewhere, filed late, or never filed) or who cannot find it. A loss from this partnership was still suspended under the passive rules in 2024 or an earlier year.
findings.why_no: The help says 'A 2024 Form 8582 (Part VII, column (c)) lists such a loss.' A filer with no such form, or who does not have it, reads that as a no.
findings.irs_text: "Enter the prior-year unallowed losses for each activity." (i8582 2025 p. 10). The carryover exists by law, whether or not a 2024 form shows it.
findings.fix: Change the help to: 'Usually shown on a 2024 Form 8582, Part VII, column (c). Answer yes even if you can't find that form, or it wasn't filed, if a loss from this partnership was ever limited by the passive activity rules and not yet used.'

findings.who: A partner with prior-year unallowed commercial revitalization deductions (CRD) from this partnership's rental real estate or other activity.
findings.why_no: A CRD carryover is a deduction, not a 'loss', and the question asks only about a loss held back.
findings.irs_text: "If you have prior-year unallowed commercial revitalization deductions (CRD) from rental real estate activities, treat that dollar amount as negative... If you have prior-year unallowed CRD from passive activities other than rental real estate activities, include that amount in Part V." (i8582 2025 p. 10)
findings.fix: Add to the help: 'Include any held-back commercial revitalization deduction (CRD).'

locators: p. 10, Part IV, "You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582"

findings.who: An individual partner who did no work in the partnership in calendar 2025 but materially participated in the partnership activity in any 5 of the prior 10 tax years, or in any 3 prior years for a personal service activity.
findings.why_no: The question asks only whether they did any work in 2025; they truthfully answer no because they did no work that year, even though the prior-year material participation tests make the activity nonpassive.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'You materially participated in the activity for any 5 tax years ... during the 10 tax years that immediately precede the tax year'; 'personal service activity and you materially participated ... for any 3 tax years ... preceding the tax year.'
findings.fix: Ask whether the filer materially participated in the activity in 2025 or under the prior-year tests, not merely whether they did work in 2025.

findings.who: A partner in a fiscal-year partnership ending in 2025 who worked in the partnership during the partnership's tax year, for example July 2024 through June 2025, but did no work during calendar 2025.
findings.why_no: They read 'In 2025' literally and answer no, although material participation is measured over the partnership's tax year.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'All determinations of material participation are based on your participation during the partnership’s tax year.'
findings.fix: Ask about work during the partnership's tax year shown on the K-1, not calendar 2025.

findings.who: A retired or disabled farmer, or the surviving spouse of a farmer, who did no work in the partnership in 2025 but is treated as materially participating under the special farmer rules.
findings.why_no: The question asks whether they did any work in 2025 and they truthfully say no; the special rule can treat them as materially participating without current-year work.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'Special rules apply to certain retired or disabled farmers and to the surviving spouses of farmers. See the Instructions for Form 8582 for details.'
findings.fix: Add a condition asking whether they are a retired or disabled farmer or surviving spouse eligible for the special material participation rule, or ask material participation rather than work.

findings.who: A real estate professional partner with a rental real estate activity reported in box 2 and no box 1 amount, who materially participated in that rental real estate activity.
findings.why_no: The gate asks only whether box 1 shows an amount; box 1 is blank, so they truthfully answer no. The gated work question is never asked even though material participation in the box 2 rental real estate activity determines whether that income or loss is nonpassive.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'You must determine if you materially participated ... (b) if you were a real estate professional ... in each rental real estate activity held through the partnership.'
findings.fix: Broaden the gate to ask work/material participation whenever the K-1 reports any trade or business or rental real estate activity amount, or ask it per activity, not only when box 1 has an amount.

findings.who: A partner in a partnership with more than one activity where box 1 is blank or nets to zero but the attached statement reports non-zero ordinary business income or loss for individual activities.
findings.why_no: They look only at box 1, see no amount or zero, and answer no; the amounts are on the required attached statement and material participation or trader status must be determined activity by activity.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'If the partnership had more than one activity, it’ll attach a statement ... specifies the income (loss), deductions, and credits from each activity'; p. 14: 'If the partnership had more than one trade or business activity, it will attach a statement identifying the income or loss from each activity.'
findings.fix: Ask whether box 1 or any attached statement shows ordinary business income or loss for any activity, and ask the trader and work questions per activity.

findings.who: A partner in a partnership that traded stocks, commodities, or other investments for its owners during the tax year but stopped trading or liquidated before the end of the year or before the return was prepared.
findings.why_no: They read the present-tense 'Is the partnership's business trading...' and answer no because the partnership is no longer trading, although the special nonpassive rule applies to income from the trading activity during the year.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 11: 'If you have net income (loss), deductions, or credits from any of the following activities, treat such amounts as nonpassive ... 3. Trading personal property for the account of owners of interests in the activity.'
findings.fix: Ask whether the partnership traded personal property for the account of its owners at any time during the partnership's tax year, not whether it is currently doing so.

findings.who: A partner in a partnership whose activity is trading personal property for its owners, but the property is not stocks, commodities, or commonly understood investments, for example other tangible personal property traded for the owners.
findings.why_no: The question lists 'stocks, commodities or other investments' and the help says a business that sells goods or services is not one; the filer answers no because the property is not on the list, even though the instructions cover trading personal property generally.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 11: 'Trading personal property for the account of owners of interests in the activity' is treated as nonpassive.
findings.fix: Use the statutory phrase 'trading personal property for the account of its owners' and do not limit the examples to stocks, commodities, or investments.

findings.who: A partner in a partnership with multiple activities, one of which trades investments for its owners and another of which sells goods or services; the filer reads 'the partnership's business' as the overall goods or services business.
findings.why_no: The help says 'a business that sells goods or services is not' a trading business; the filer answers no for the whole partnership, missing that the trading activity itself is covered.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: multiple-activity statement identifies each activity; p. 11: 'Trading personal property for the account of owners of interests in the activity' is nonpassive.
findings.fix: Ask whether any activity of the partnership is trading personal property for its owners, and make the question activity-specific when a statement is attached.

findings.who: A partner who regularly checks on the partnership's operations in a managerial capacity but is not involved day-to-day; the help says 'checking on it as an investor does not count.'
findings.why_no: They read the help as excluding all checking or monitoring and answer no, although the IRS text excludes investor monitoring only when it is non-managerial and not directly involved in day-to-day operations.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: work as an investor is not counted if 'you aren’t directly involved in the day-to-day operations'; examples include 'Monitoring the finances or operations of the activity in a non-managerial capacity.'
findings.fix: Clarify that managerial oversight and checking operations in a managerial capacity count; only passive, non-managerial investor monitoring does not.

findings.who: A partner who did substantial clerical, bookkeeping, or maintenance work in the partnership but reads 'Count work in running the business' as counting only management or executive work.
findings.why_no: The help narrows the question to 'running the business,' so they answer no even though the IRS text generally counts any work in connection with the activity, subject to the investor and tax-avoidance exclusions.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'Generally, any work that you or your spouse does in connection with an activity held through a partnership ... is counted toward material participation.'
findings.fix: Say any work in connection with the activity counts, not just management work, except for the specific investor and tax-avoidance exclusions.

findings.who: A partner in a partnership that holds an interest in a lower-tier operating entity; the filer works for the operating entity, not directly for the K-1 partnership.
findings.why_no: They answer no to work 'in the partnership's business' because they did not work for the upper-tier partnership itself, although work in connection with an activity held through the partnership counts.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: work counted includes 'any work that you or your spouse does in connection with an activity held through a partnership.'
findings.fix: Ask about work in connection with the activity held through the partnership, including work for a lower-tier or operating entity that carries on the activity.

findings.who: A filer whose box 1 shows a loss in parentheses and who reads 'Does box 1 show an amount?' as asking about positive income, despite the parenthetical 'income or loss.'
findings.why_no: They treat a negative figure as a loss rather than an amount and answer no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 14: 'The amount reported in box 1 is your share of the ordinary income (loss) ...'
findings.fix: Say explicitly that a loss shown in parentheses or with a minus sign is an amount for this question.

locators: p. 11, Special rules for certain other activities, "Trading personal property for the account of owners of interests in the activity"
p. 14, Box 1. Ordinary Business Income (Loss), "The amount reported in box 1 is your share of the ordinary income (loss) from trade or business activities of the partnership"
p. 9, Work counted toward material participation, "any work that you or your spouse does in connection with an activity held through a partnership"

findings.who: A general partner whose Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 14 shows code A with a negative figure, for example (12,400) or -12,400, because the partnership's trade or business had a loss.
findings.why_no: The gate's parenthetical says only "(net earnings from self-employment)", without "(loss)". A partner with a loss reads "net earnings" as positive income, decides there are no earnings, and answers no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 22, Code A: "Net earnings (loss) from self-employment. ... If the amount in this box is a loss, enter only the deductible amount on Schedule SE (Form 1040)."
findings.fix: Ask: "Does box 14 show any amount with code A (net earnings or loss from self-employment), including a negative amount or an amount in parentheses?"

findings.who: A partner whose box 14 code A shows a loss, and who knows from the basis, at-risk or passive limits that the loss is not deductible this year.
findings.why_no: The gate cites "enter only the deductible amount on Schedule SE." A partner with no deductible amount concludes there is nothing to report and answers no. The question then never collects the loss "before any change", so the tool cannot apply the limitation itself.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 22, Code A: "If the amount in this box is a loss, enter only the deductible amount on Schedule SE (Form 1040). See Limitations on Losses, Deductions, and Credits, earlier."
findings.fix: State in the help: "Answer yes if any amount appears with code A, even a loss you think you cannot deduct. The tool applies the limits later." Cite the box contents, not the Schedule SE entry rule.

findings.who: A partner whose box 14 shows "A" followed by "STMT", "*" or "See attached", with the dollar amount (or several code A amounts, one per activity) printed only on the partnership's attached statement.
findings.why_no: The words "does box 14 show an amount" read literally: the box itself shows no number, only a reference to a statement, so the partner answers no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 22, Code A: "Net earnings (loss) from self-employment." The amount reported with code A is the partner's share, whether it is printed in the box or on a supporting statement.
findings.fix: Ask: "Does box 14 list code A, with an amount either in the box or on an attached statement the box refers to?" In the amount help, say to total all code A amounts from the statement.

findings.who: A partner who receives a corrected or amended Schedule K-1 (Form 1065), where the original showed no code A but the corrected one does, or the reverse.
findings.why_no: "On this Schedule K-1" does not say which version to use. A partner who looks at the original, or the one first entered, answers no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 22, Code A: "Net earnings (loss) from self-employment". The amount is the one the partnership reports to the partner for the year.
findings.fix: Add to the help: "If you received a corrected Schedule K-1, use the corrected one."

locators: p. 22, Code A. Net earnings (loss) from self-employment, "If the amount in this box is a loss, enter only the deductible amount on Schedule SE"

findings.who: A partner whose K-1 from a large or publicly traded partnership prints only "O" with "STMT" or "*" in box 15. The backup withholding dollar amount appears only on the attached supplemental statement.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether box 15 "show[s] an amount" with code O. The box itself shows no number, only a code and a reference to a statement. A literal reader answers no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 23, Code O: "This is your share of the credit for backup withholding on dividends, interest income, and other types of income. Include this amount in the total you enter on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 25c"
findings.fix: Ask: "Does box 15 list code O (backup withholding), either with an amount or with a note such as STMT or * pointing to an attached statement?" Then ask for the amount from the box or the statement.

findings.who: A partner who received an original K-1 with no code O, then a corrected or amended K-1 from the partnership that adds backup withholding in box 15 code O.
findings.why_no: "On this Schedule K-1" can lead the filer to answer from the first K-1 received instead of the final corrected one.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 23, Code O: "Include this amount in the total you enter on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 25c"
findings.fix: Add help: "If the partnership sent a corrected Schedule K-1, answer from the corrected one."

findings.who: Joint filers where only the spouse is a partner and the spouse's K-1 shows box 15 code O backup withholding.
findings.why_no: The per-document question may be answered only for the K-1s the filer thinks of as their own. A spouse's K-1 may never be entered, or may be answered no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 23, Code O: "Include this amount in the total you enter on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 25c"
findings.fix: When the K-1 list is collected, ask about Schedules K-1 (Form 1065) issued to "you or your spouse."

locators: p. 23, Code O. Backup withholding, "Include this amount in the total you enter on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 25c"

findings.who: A partner whose K-1 box 18 shows code A with "STMT" or "*" instead of a dollar figure, and the tax-exempt interest amount appears only on an attached statement. This is common for large or tiered partnerships whose box 18 entries do not fit on the face of the form.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether box 18 "show[s] an amount with code A". The box itself shows only "STMT", not an amount, so the filer answers no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 25, Code A: "Report on your return, as an item of information, your share of the tax-exempt interest received or accrued by the partnership during the year. Individual partners include this amount on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 2a."
findings.fix: Ask: "Does box 18 of this K-1, or a statement attached to it for box 18, show code A (tax-exempt interest income)? Answer yes if box 18 says STMT or * and the statement lists code A." Then ask for the total code A amount, adding any entries listed on the statement.

findings.who: A partner whose K-1 shows more than one code A entry in box 18. Partnerships do this, for example, to separate in-state from out-of-state municipal interest, or private activity bond interest from other interest.
findings.why_no: The filer answers yes to the gate. The gated question then asks for "The amount in box 18 with code A" (singular), so the filer enters only the first figure and drops the rest. The silent loss is the same as with a false no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 25, Code A: "your share of the tax-exempt interest received or accrued by the partnership during the year"
findings.fix: Reword the gated question: "The total of all box 18 code A amounts on this K-1 and any attached statement."

findings.who: Any filer who answers yes to the gate.
findings.why_no: The line's Choose step repeats the gate in a helper ("Box 18 shows an amount with code A" = false → Zero). Under the gate, that branch cannot be reached. If the helper is ever wired to a different input than k1p.has_b18a, the line could fall to zero after a yes.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 25, Code A: "Individual partners include this amount on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 2a."
findings.fix: Under the gate, define the line directly as k1p.box18a and remove the redundant helper branch.

locators: p. 25, Code A. Tax-exempt interest income, "Individual partners include this amount on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 2a"

findings.who: A partner whose partnership enters '*' or 'STMT' in box 19 and lists the codes and amounts on an attached statement. Large investment partnerships often do this.
findings.why_no: Box 19 itself holds no number, only a code letter or 'see statement', so 'Does box 19 (distributions) show an amount?' is truthfully no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 25, Box 19: 'The partnership will also attach a statement separately identifying the following...' (distributions reported by code, with supporting statements)
findings.fix: Ask: 'Does box 19 of this Schedule K-1, or any statement attached for box 19, show a distribution code or an amount (including "STMT" or "*")?'

findings.who: A partner whose share of partnership liabilities went down during 2025, for example when the partnership paid down a mortgage or refinanced away recourse debt. The partnership did not enter code D in box 19, and the drop appears only in Item K (beginning versus ending liabilities).
findings.why_no: No cash came out and box 19 is blank, so the filer truthfully answers no. A decrease in liability share is a deemed distribution of money under section 752(b) and can exceed basis.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 25, Box 19, Code A: 'Code A, however, doesn't include deemed distributions of money under section 752(b); see Code D, later.' Also 'To the extent the cash ... received exceed the adjusted basis of your partnership interest immediately before the distribution, the excess is treated as gain'
findings.fix: Broaden the gate: 'Does box 19 show any code or amount, OR did your share of liabilities in Item K go down from the beginning to the end of the year?' Treat a Yes to the Item K part as a possible deemed distribution and route it to the basis comparison.

findings.who: A partner who received property with a zero (or fully reduced) partnership basis. Box 19 shows code C (or code B) with 0, or code A for marketable securities reduced to zero by the section 731(c)(3)(B) reduction amount.
findings.why_no: The box shows a code but the amount is 0, so 'show an amount' reads as no. Yet a code other than A should end the interview.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 25, Box 19, Code C: 'Code C is used to report the partnership's adjusted basis in property other than money immediately before the property was distributed to you'
findings.fix: Ask whether box 19 shows any code letter (A, B, C, D, E, F, G), even with a zero or blank amount, rather than 'an amount'.

findings.who: A partner who received only property or a payment for services (code C, F or G) and no cash.
findings.why_no: The gate's citation and help center on code A, 'Cash and marketable securities'. A filer can read 'distributions' as money only and answer no when box 19 shows only non-money codes.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 25, Box 19, Code C: 'Other property' and Code A: 'doesn't include distributions the partnership made to you for performing services. See the instructions later for codes F and G.'
findings.fix: State in the help: 'Answer yes if box 19 shows any code, including property (C), section 737 property (B), liability decreases (D), or services (F, G), not only cash.'

locators: p. 25, Box 19. Distributions, "Code A. Cash and marketable securities other than for services"

p. 25, Box 19. Distributions, "exceed the adjusted basis of your partnership interest immediately before the distribution, the excess is treated as gain from the sale or exchange of your partnership interest"

findings.who: A partner who is a real estate professional and materially participated in the partnership's rental real estate activity. Their K-1 shows a figure in box 2.
findings.why_no: The help quoted with the gate says box 2 is 'a passive activity amount for all partners.' A partner who knows their activity is nonpassive may decide the box-2 question does not apply to them and answer no, even though the box shows a number.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 14, Box 2: 'the income (loss) in box 2 isn't from a passive activity if you were a real estate professional ... and you materially participated ... report box 2 income (loss) in column (i) or (k) of Schedule E (Form 1040), line 28.'
findings.fix: Keep the gate to the printed fact and change the help to say: 'Answer yes if any number other than zero is printed in box 2, whether income or a loss, and whether or not the activity is passive to you. Passive treatment is decided later.'

findings.who: A partner whose box 2 shows a loss printed in parentheses, such as (4,200), or with a minus sign.
findings.why_no: The gate's words 'show an amount' may be read as income only. A filer may not count a bracketed loss as an amount and answer no, which drops a loss the return should report or limit through Form 8582.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 14, Box 2: 'If you have a loss from a passive activity in box 2 ... report the loss in column (g) of Schedule E (Form 1040), line 28' / 'follow the Instructions for Form 8582.'
findings.fix: Reword the gate as: 'Does box 2 show any amount other than zero, either income or a loss (a loss may be shown in parentheses or with a minus sign)?'

findings.who: A partner in a partnership with several rental real estate activities. The K-1 has an asterisk or a reference to an attached statement that lists the amount for each activity.
findings.why_no: The filer sees a statement reference instead of a single plain figure, or looks only at the statement. They may conclude that box 2 itself does not 'show an amount' and answer no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 14, Box 2: 'If the partnership had more than one rental real estate activity, it'll attach a statement identifying the income or loss from each activity.'
findings.fix: Add to the help: 'Answer yes if box 2 shows a total, or if the partnership's attached statement reports net rental real estate income or loss for box 2.'

locators: p. 14, Box 2. Net Rental Real Estate Income (Loss), "Generally, the income (loss) reported in box 2 is a passive activity amount for all partners"

findings.who: A partner in a partnership, often a publicly traded partnership or a large fund, whose K-1 box 20 has more codes than fit. Box 20 shows only an asterisk or "STMT", and the supplemental statement lists code Z with per-business QBI, W-2 wages and UBIA.
